column1: # condens-state.tsv — OBSERVED state of published Condens artifacts.
# WRITTEN BY AN AGENT, READ BY A SCRIPT. This split is the whole design.
# check-condens.sh runs in CI with no credentials and cannot reach Condens. So the
# loop has two halves:
#   FETCH   an agent with the Condens connector lists published artifacts, writes this
#           file, AND saves each artifact's text to condens-cache/<artifact_id>.md.
#           A ritual, not a build step — it needs a session and credentials.
#   CHECK   check-condens.sh compares what EVIDENCE.md claims against what this file
#           observed. No network, works in CI, fails honestly when this file is stale.
# THE CONTENT IS THE POINT, NOT THIS TABLE. updatedAt alone cannot tell a typo fix
# from a reversed finding, so the fetch must save the text. check-condens.sh hashes
# the cache against condens-reconciled/ — the version a human signed off — and
# isolates whether the FIGURES moved. Without the cache it falls back to comparing
# these dates and says so. Saving metadata only is the weak half of the ritual.
# RECONCILIATION IS THE OTHER HALF, and it is a human act:
#     # read what changed, then record what you read
#     mkdir -p condens-reconciled && cp condens-cache/*.md condens-reconciled/
#     # and set reconciled_at: in the gate files to today
# Copying without reading defeats the entire check. Nothing can detect that.
# Deliberately NOT an API call from the script: a check that passes only when
# somebody's token is valid fails for reasons unrelated to what it measures, and
# teams learn to ignore it. Here the failure mode is legible instead — "this
# observation is N days old" is a different sentence from "the artifact moved."
# Columns: share_id <TAB> artifact_id <TAB> updated_at <TAB> name
